body.text: What is clear is that the later it gets, the fewer options remain. Once you are indicted, the option of a suspended indictment has already passed.
Still, avoid contacting the victim on day one

That said, calling the victim the day after the incident usually backfires. Contact received while the victim is still angry sounds more like pressure than an apology. Investigators, too, do not look favorably on a suspect contacting the victim directly. If the first contact begins with talk of money, it also easily leaves the impression that you are trying to buy your way out.

If you are disputing the charge, you need to be even more careful. Raising a settlement hastily can look as though you have admitted the facts. The proper order is to decide first which parts to dispute and which to admit, and to begin settlement talks within that direction. In a case where you dispute some parts and admit others, one approach is to start by discussing compensation for the parts you admit.

When you receive a settlement agreement, check that it contains a sentence saying the victim does not want you punished, and that the case number and date are correct. A settlement agreement only counts if it is submitted promptly to wherever the case currently is, that is, the police, the Public Prosecution Office (공소청) or the court. Receiving it and keeping it in a drawer does no good.
When you do not know how to reach the victim

If you do not know the victim's contact details, do not ask around to track them down and visit them. If you ask the investigator in charge to pass on that you wish to settle, contact will follow if the victim agrees. If you have appointed defense counsel, asking the victim's side about their wishes through counsel first puts less pressure on both sides.

The victim may ultimately not want to settle. In that case, the next step is to respect that wish while keeping a record of your attempts to settle and your efforts to make up for the harm. After indictment you can consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁), but because it is money deposited regardless of the victim's wishes, you should also know before deciding that it is often not given the same weight as a settlement.

author: kim-hansol

title: How diet pills bought directly from overseas become ‘importing psychotropics’
summary: Appetite suppressants and sleep aids sold freely abroad may contain ingredients classified as psychotropic drugs in Korea. We explain why buying them directly from overseas leads to the import provision, which is heavier than possession.

body.text: Some medicines that can only be obtained in Korea with a doctor's prescription are sold like health foods in overseas online stores. Quite a few people order them because they are cheaper and more convenient, and then get a call from customs. The first thing to know in these cases is that, even for the same medicine, different provisions apply to holding it in Korea and to bringing it in from abroad.
Even category (d) drugs are a step heavier when imported

If a person who is not a narcotics handler possesses category (d) psychotropic drugs (향정 라목), such as zolpidem or phentermine, the penalty is imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to 50 million won (Article 61(1)5 of the Narcotics Control Act (마약류관리법)). But if the same medicine is brought in from abroad, it becomes importing, and the penalty rises to imprisonment of up to ten years or a fine of up to 100 million won (Article 60(1)3).

If the ingredient is a category (a) or (b) psychotropic drug or cannabis, importing carries life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least five years, and for category (c), imprisonment for a definite term of at least one year. So in direct-purchase cases, you can only know the statutory penalty once you have checked which category the tested ingredient falls into, not the product name.

The value threshold must be checked as well. If the value of imported psychotropic drugs exceeds 5 million won, the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄가중처벌법) may apply, so if you placed several orders, first check the total amount.
Inspection of directly purchased foods has become tighter

With the amendment to the Special Act on Imported Food Safety Control that took effect on January 1, 2026, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety is now required to inspect overseas direct-purchase foods that may contain narcotic raw materials or ingredients. Jellies or drinks containing cannabis ingredients, and products sold abroad as health foods, are that much more likely to be caught at customs clearance.

The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety provides a service, Overseas Direct Purchase Food Guide (해외직구식품 올바로), where you can check raw materials and ingredients that are blocked from entry. Many cases could be avoided simply by searching the ingredient name once before ordering.

Sometimes customs contacts you and asks you to agree to disposal, but agreeing to disposal does not end the case. Goods confirmed to contain narcotic ingredients may be reported to investigators separately from disposal, and the answers you gave over the phone at that time are later reviewed together with your statements.
Explain that you did not know with the purchase screens

The crime of importing also requires intent, so if you did not know the product contained narcotic ingredients, you can dispute the charge. The description on the sales page, the ingredient labeling, the price, purchase reviews and your search history before and after ordering are the materials for that judgment. Conversely, if the seller used slang or told you to split your orders because customs clearance was difficult, these are circumstances suggesting that you knew.

items: Order history and screens of the product page (save them; do not delete them)
Payment records and conversations with any purchasing agent
Medical records, if you were taking the same medicine on a prescription in Korea
A summary of whether you had ordered the same item before

body.text: If it was for treatment, your medical records in Korea become important material. If you can explain whether you were seeing a doctor for the same symptoms and why you chose to buy directly from overseas, it becomes easier to show that you brought it in solely for your own use.

author: kim-hansol

title: Why a ‘THC 0’ label does not work in Korea
summary: CBD oils and gummies sold abroad like health foods are cannabis under Korean law. We set out why they are treated as cannabis regardless of THC content, and how the applicable provision changes depending on how the product was brought in.

body.text: After the autumn travel season, similar inquiries keep coming in: someone bought CBD gummies said to help with sleep at a supermarket abroad and was caught at the airport, or someone got a call from customs because of CBD oil they received as a gift. They feel wronged, saying the package stated there was no THC, but that label is not the standard under Korean law.
CBD is cannabis in itself

The Narcotics Control Act (마약류관리법) defines cannabis as the cannabis plant and its resin, products made from them as raw materials, chemically synthesized equivalents specified by Presidential Decree, and mixtures containing any of these (Article 2, item 4). The Enforcement Decree specifies cannabidiol (CBD) as cannabis, together with cannabinol (CBN) and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) (Annex 7-2 of the Enforcement Decree).

So if a product contains CBD, it is cannabis whatever its THC content. The law excludes the seeds, roots and mature stalks of the cannabis plant and products made from them, but even a product labeled as extracted from stalks or seeds is treated as a mixture containing cannabis if it contains CBD.

The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety's guidance on narcotics also describes cannabis as the cannabis plant and its resin, cannabinol, tetrahydrocannabinol and cannabidiol. If the ingredient list of a foreign product shows CBD, cannabidiol or hemp extract, it is safer to treat it as a product containing cannabis ingredients.
How it was brought in decides the penalty

If you brought it in your luggage or received it through a direct overseas purchase, it is importing cannabis. The statutory penalty is life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least five years (Article 58(1)5), so the starting point differs from possessing a product received in Korea, which carries imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to 50 million won (Article 61(1)6). If you received it as a gift from a friend living in Korea, it may be treated as a matter of receiving and possession, but if you asked the friend to bring it in or were involved in the process, being an accomplice to importing may come up.

The sentencing guidelines treat importing for one's own use as a special mitigating factor. If you bought it for sleep or pain, you need to show it was for personal use by setting out records of treatment for those symptoms, the quantity ordered and whether purchases were repeated.
Buying it in a country where it is legal, and not knowing

The fact that it was legal in the country where it was sold does not change the judgment under Korean law. If you knew it contained CBD but did not know that was prohibited, it becomes a question of mistake of law, and you escape punishment only if there was a justifiable reason for that belief (Article 16 of the Criminal Act). This standard is not easily met, so it is realistic to also prepare to explain the circumstances at the disposition and sentencing stages.

For cannabis-based medicines that are truly necessary for treatment, there is a separate route: obtaining them through the Korea Orphan & Essential Drug Center, or carrying them in and out of the country for self-treatment with the approval of the Minister of Food and Drug Safety (Article 3(3) of the Enforcement Decree). Products bought from overseas online stores are not regarded as having gone through this procedure, even if a doctor recommended them. Foods made from seeds, such as hemp seed oil, can be distributed only within the limits for trace residues, and oils or capsules marketed for CBD fall outside that range.

author: kim-hansol

title: With cannabis, ‘buying’ can be heavier than smoking
summary: Smoking cannabis falls under a provision that allows a fine, but buying and selling can be dealt with under a provision carrying imprisonment of at least one year. We also look at what happens if you bought a friend's share as well.

body.text: In consultations on cannabis cases, many people start by saying, ‘I only smoked it a few times.’ But the weight of a cannabis case is sometimes decided more by how the cannabis was obtained and to whom it was passed than by the number of times it was smoked. This is because, even with the same cannabis, the applicable provision differs completely depending on the act.
Smoking and trading are in different provisions

Smoking cannabis, or possessing it for the purpose of smoking, carries imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to 50 million won (Article 61(1)4 of the Narcotics Control Act (마약류관리법)). Cultivation, possession, receiving and transporting are also in the same Article 61. By contrast, buying or selling cannabis, or arranging or encouraging its sale, falls under Article 59(1)7, with no fine option and imprisonment for a definite term of at least one year.

The difference between the two provisions is more than numbers. Under a provision that allows a fine, a first offender with few occasions has a relatively wide chance of the case ending with a suspended indictment or a fine. Under a provision with a minimum of one year, a fine cannot be chosen, so if the case goes to trial you argue for a suspended sentence on the premise of imprisonment.

In practice, buying cannabis is sometimes treated as trading and this provision is applied. That is why, in cases where a seller is caught and the list of buyers is handed over, buying becomes an issue as well as smoking.

In Telegram transactions where transfer records and chats remain, the number of purchases is fully exposed. Rather than giving a lower or higher number from memory, the first step is to check each transaction in the records one by one and see whether any transfers unrelated to you are mixed in.
If you bought a friend's share as well

It is common for one person to buy on behalf of several people who plan to smoke together. The part bought from the seller can be treated as trading, and the part passed on to friends is trading if you received payment, or receiving and giving if you simply gave it. If there are transfer records, you first need to sort out whether that money was payment for cannabis or a split of shared expenses.

This distinction carries through to the sentence. In the trading and brokering category, the sentencing guidelines for drug crimes list ‘buying or receiving for use, simple possession and the like’ as a special mitigating factor. If it is accepted that you bought solely for your own use, even the same purchase may be assessed differently.
It is different if the other person is a minor

Giving cannabis to a minor or having a minor smoke it carries imprisonment for a definite term of at least two years (Article 58-2(1)). If anyone in the group was a minor, that fact must be checked first. Since the weight of the case depends on which act it is classified as, the first task is to write down smoking, buying and sharing separately, by date and by person.

If the cannabis was brought in from abroad, yet another provision awaits. Importing cannabis carries life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least five years (Article 58(1)5), which is far heavier than buying it in Korea. This is why you also need to check whether any cannabis products received through direct overseas purchase are mixed in.

author: kim-hansol

title: It is ‘importing’ even if you did not carry it in yourself
summary: Drugs ordered from an overseas seller and received by mail also amount to the crime of importing, and the statutory penalty starts from a different point than buying in Korea. We look at the scope of the crime of importing and the aggravation thresholds.

body.text: When people hear ‘smuggling’, they tend to picture bags being searched at the airport. But most importing cases we see in consultations are not that dramatic. An item ordered from an overseas website is caught at customs while coming by international mail, and a few days later investigators get in touch. The person thinks they merely bought something, but the law treats it as importing.
It is importing the moment it enters the country

Importing narcotics means bringing narcotics into Korea. It is importing not only when you carry them in yourself but also when you order from an overseas seller and receive them by post or express courier, and the fact that you brought them in for your own use does not, on its own, stop it being importing.

So even for the same quantity, the statutory penalty is far heavier than for buying in Korea. Smoking cannabis carries imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to 50 million won, but importing cannabis carries life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least five years (Article 58(1)5 of the Narcotics Control Act (마약류관리법)). Importing category (b) psychotropics such as methamphetamine, category (a) such as LSD, or narcotics all likewise carry life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least five years.

items: Importing narcotics, category (a) or (b) psychotropics, or cannabis: life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least five years (Article 58(1))
Importing category (c) psychotropics: imprisonment for a definite term of at least one year (Article 59(1)10)
Importing category (d) psychotropics such as zolpidem: imprisonment of up to ten years or a fine of up to 100 million won (Article 60(1)3)

body.text: Even if you never received it, even if you only prepared

Even if it was caught at customs and you never received it, you can be punished for attempted importing (Article 58(3)). Preparation and conspiracy for the crimes in Article 58(1) are also punishable by imprisonment of up to ten years (paragraph (4)), so whether it is a completed offense, an attempt or preparation depends on what you did at which stage, from ordering and paying to specifying the delivery address.

When narcotics are found in international mail or express cargo at customs clearance, investigators sometimes deliver the item as is and identify the recipient. Courts regard opening and inspection for customs clearance as an administrative investigation, so it is hard to have evidence excluded merely because the package was opened without a warrant. Instead, the seizure procedure after receipt and the way the recipient was identified can be examined.

There are value thresholds as well. If the value of imported narcotics or psychotropic drugs is 5 million won or more, Article 11(1) of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄가중처벌법) applies, with life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least seven years, and if it is 50 million won or more, life imprisonment or imprisonment of at least ten years. Importing cannabis is not covered by this provision.
In the end, it is a question of what you knew

The crime of importing also requires intent. The first thing disputed is whether you knew it was a narcotic, or at least ordered or received it while thinking it might be. Circumstances such as whether the seller used slang, whether they explained ways to avoid customs, and whether the price was unusually high become the materials for that judgment.

The sentencing guidelines treat importing solely for one's own use as a special mitigating factor in the import and export category. But if you ordered the same item several times or the quantity was enough to share with others, it is hard to have this accepted, so the entire order history should be checked first.

author: kim-hansol

title: Why subway groping cases fall under Article 11 of the Sexual Violence Punishment Act
summary: Cases on the morning commute are often investigated not as indecent assault under the Criminal Act but under Article 11 of the Sexual Violence Punishment Act. The two provisions differ in their requirements, statutory penalties and punishment of attempts.

body.text: The summons text message received by someone reported on the subway usually gives a long charge name: ‘Violation of the Sexual Violence Punishment Act (Indecent Act in a Crowded Public Place)’. Many people ask how this differs from indecent assault. The answer is that even the same physical contact can fall under a different provision because of where it happened.
The provisions require different things

Indecent assault under Article 298 of the Criminal Act requires an indecent act committed by violence or intimidation. By contrast, Article 11 of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes (성폭력처벌법) is satisfied when a person commits an indecent act against another on public transport, at a performance or assembly venue, or in any other place where the public is crowded together, and does not separately require violence or intimidation. The law recognizes separately that these are spaces where crowds make it hard for victims to move away and easy for offenders to pretend it was an accident.

The statutory penalties differ too. Indecent assault carries imprisonment of up to ten years or a fine of up to 15 million won, while Article 11 carries imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to 30 million won. The cap on imprisonment is lower under Article 11, but the cap on fines is actually higher. If there are clear signs of touching someone's body by surprise, indecent assault may be considered even on the subway, so you first need to confirm which provision you are being investigated under.

A crowded public place does not mean only subways and buses. The provision gives performance venues and assembly sites as examples and adds any other place where the public is crowded together. Whether a place qualifies, such as a festival site, a packed elevator or a store with a long queue, can be disputed depending on the nature of the place and the circumstances at the time.
There is no provision punishing attempts

Article 15 of the Sexual Violence Punishment Act limits the punishment of attempts to Articles 3 to 9, 14, 14-2 and 14-3. Article 11 is not among them. This means that in a case where someone reached out but was stopped before making contact, they cannot be punished for an attempted Article 11 offense. Because the Criminal Act does punish attempted indecent assault (Article 300 of the Criminal Act), this difference means the applicable provision can change the size of the case.
In the end, it is about intent and movements

What is most often disputed in Article 11 cases is whether the contact was deliberate. Being pushed against someone on a crowded train and deliberately pressing a hand or body against them lead to different conclusions. Investigators look at CCTV in the train and station, the position of the hands, the duration of contact and behavior right after getting off. Materials that explain your posture, such as the station where you boarded and got off, transit card records and the bag you were carrying at the time, become hard to obtain as time passes.

If you were caught on the spot and taken to a police box, the statement you wrote there becomes the backbone of the case. Sentences written in panic, such as “I'm sorry” or “I think I touched her,” are easily read later as admitting intent. If you have already written a statement, first write down from memory what you put in it.

One misunderstanding needs correcting. A statutory penalty lighter than indecent assault does not mean the ancillary measures are light. Under Article 11, too, once a fine becomes final you become subject to registration of personal information, and completion orders and employment restrictions are also decided. That is how far apart a suspended indictment and a fine are.

author: kim-hansol

title: Can photographing someone fully clothed be illegal filming?
summary: The crime of filming with a camera or similar device starts from whether what was filmed is a body part that may arouse sexual desire or shame. We set out the factors courts consider, the punishment of attempts and possession, and why forensics can change the size of a case.

body.text: When people think of illegal filming, they tend to picture hidden cameras in toilets or changing rooms. But there are also quite a few cases of photographing someone in leggings on the street or filming the legs of the person sitting opposite on the subway. That is why people ask whether it can be a crime when nothing was exposed.
The body as the law defines it

Article 14(1) of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes (성폭력처벌법) punishes a person who films the body of another that may arouse sexual desire or shame, against the will of the person filmed, with imprisonment of up to seven years or a fine of up to 50 million won. The provision does not make exposure a requirement. It is structured to ask what the footage means, rather than what exactly was filmed.

Courts judge from the standpoint of an average person of the same sex and age group as the victim, considering a range of circumstances together. Even if the person was clothed, it may qualify if a particular body part was zoomed in on or the person was followed and filmed repeatedly from behind. On the other hand, if a person was merely included in a landscape or an ordinary photo of people, there is room for dispute.

items: The victim's clothing and degree of exposure
The intent of the person filming and how the filming came about
The place, angle and distance of the filming
Whether a particular body part was emphasized in the shot

body.text: Even if the filming was not completed, even if it was deleted

Article 14 also punishes attempts (Article 15 of the Sexual Violence Punishment Act). If filming has begun, for example by putting a phone under a skirt, it can be an attempt even if no file was saved. The crime is complete the moment the filming takes place, so deleting it later does not make it as if it never happened, and deleted files are often recovered through forensics.

You can be punished even if you did not do the filming yourself. Possessing, purchasing, storing or viewing the footage or copies of it carries imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to 30 million won (Article 14(4)). If you forwarded a video you received to another group chat, it is assessed as providing or distributing it, and the same statutory penalty as filming applies.

Videos filmed between partners are no exception. Whether there was consent at the time of filming is assessed scene by scene. Even if filming took place several times with consent, a single occasion without consent is a separate problem, and knowing that one was being filmed is not the same as consenting to the filming.
Other files on the phone make the case bigger

In illegal filming cases, the phone is the most important evidence. If old photos unrelated to the current report are also found, separate cases are added, and if the conduct is assessed as habitual, the sentence can be increased by up to one half (Article 14(5)). If you are asked at the scene to submit your phone voluntarily, you need to state not only whether you will submit it but also the scope, in terms of which period and which apps' data.

For filming with a camera or similar device, you become subject to registration of personal information even if a fine becomes final. This differs from offenses such as obscene acts using communication media, where a fine takes you out of registration, so how seriously the possibility of a suspended indictment is pursued at the disposition stage changes the outcome. Whether the filmed scene is a body as the law defines it is the first issue in that.

author: kim-hansol

title: The investigator's first call: what you must write down
summary: Calls asking you to come in for questioning usually come without warning. We set out what to note down on the first call, what to hold back, and what not to do in the 30 minutes after you hang up.

body.text: When a call from an unknown number begins with the words ‘This is the investigation team at the police station’, most people's minds go blank. When we hear about that call in the consultation room, quite a few people say they were so startled that they explained their situation at length on the spot. When a summons is made by phone, an investigation report stating its purpose is attached to the case file (Article 19(4) of the Investigation Rules (수사준칙)), and what you said on the call can remain as the first impression of the case. Wanting to explain yourself is natural, but at that moment you do not yet even know what the case is about.
What to write down is fixed

items: The charge and the case number
The department in charge, the investigator's name and direct number
Whether the case began with a complaint, a report at the scene, or grew out of another case
The date, time and place the investigator proposed for your appearance

body.text: In principle, a summons is made with a written summons stating the gist of the alleged facts, and it may be made by phone or text message when there are urgent circumstances (Article 19(3) of the Investigation Rules). So asking for the gist of why you are being called is a natural question. Even if you cannot hear the details over the phone, knowing just the charge greatly changes the direction of your preparation.
Also ask whether you are being called as a suspect or as a witness. Some people are contacted as witnesses and become suspects partway through questioning, so neither should be taken lightly.
You do not have to confirm the date on the spot

Investigators must agree the date, time and place of questioning with the suspect, and with defense counsel if there is one (Article 19(2) of the Investigation Rules). If you request a postponement, they are to adjust it unless there are special circumstances. Saying you will call back after consulting a lawyer is not an evasive answer; it is an answer within the procedure.

Cutting off contact or failing to appear without reason is another story. If you do not comply with a summons without a justifiable reason, an arrest warrant may be requested (Article 200-2 of the Criminal Procedure Act). Investigators also distinguish between postponing a schedule and avoiding the investigation. If it is difficult to appear because of work commitments or medical treatment, it is better to say so honestly. There is also a provision allowing questioning outside the investigating office where it is extremely difficult to appear at the police station because of treatment or similar reasons (Article 19(5) of the Investigation Rules).
The 30 minutes after you hang up

When the call ends, you will want to contact the other person and ask what is going on. That one message often becomes the most unfavorable piece of evidence in the case. The same goes for asking mutual acquaintances about the situation. Regardless of your intent, it can be read as an attempt to get stories straight, and clearing out chat rooms or deleting photos also often happens in exactly this window.

Those 30 minutes are better spent writing down what you remember. Write down when, where and with whom you were, as it comes to mind, and mark which parts are certain and which are hazy. Save a screenshot of the summons text message, and if it was a call, note the time of the call and what the investigator said. These notes become the starting point for consultation and preparing for questioning.

author: kim-hansol

title: Divorcing a foreign spouse: which country's law applies?
summary: If your spouse is a foreign national, you first need to check whether you can divorce in a Korean court and which country's law applies. We set out the jurisdiction and governing law provisions of the Act on Private International Law, service of documents, and recognition of judgments.

body.text: As international marriages increase, divorce consultations involving foreign spouses come in steadily. Many people tell us their spouse returned to their home country and contact was lost, or that it seems the spouse never intended to live in Korea in the first place. In such cases, there are two things to check before looking at the grounds for divorce: whether a Korean court can take the case, and under which country's law it will be decided.
Can a Korean court take the case?

Article 56 of the Act on Private International Law (국제사법) sets out when Korean courts have jurisdiction in matrimonial cases. These include cases where one spouse's habitual residence is in Korea and the couple's last common habitual residence was also in Korea, where the plaintiff and minor children have their habitual residence in Korea, where both spouses are Korean nationals, and where a Korean national with habitual residence in Korea files suit solely to dissolve the marriage.

If you lived together in Korea and your foreign spouse left home, Korean courts will usually have jurisdiction. Conversely, if both spouses live abroad or both are foreign nationals, each case has to be reviewed separately.

Jurisdiction affects not only the divorce but also matters concerning children and property. If your child is growing up in Korea, the person with parental authority (친권자) and the custodial parent can also be decided by the Korean court, but if property in your spouse's name is abroad, there are limits to enforcing a Korean judgment against it. Even if the divorce itself is settled easily in Korea, actually receiving a division of property and child support often remains a separate task.
Under which country's law is it decided?

Article 66 of the Act on Private International Law provides that divorce is governed, in order, by the law of the spouses' common nationality, the law of their common habitual residence, and the law of the place most closely connected, while providing that Korean law applies if one spouse is a Korean national with habitual residence in Korea. So for a Korean spouse living in Korea, the grounds for divorce are decided under Article 840 of the Civil Act. How divorce works in the other spouse's country is not an issue at this stage.
Service of documents and what comes after the judgment

If you do not know your spouse's address, you show that service by ordinary means is impossible and proceed by service by public notice (공시송달). The first service by public notice takes effect after two weeks, and service by public notice for service to be made abroad after two months, and these periods cannot be shortened (Article 196 of the Civil Procedure Act). If you know the foreign address, service must go through overseas service, which can take several months.

items: Check your spouse's name in Roman letters, date of birth and passport number in the documents submitted when the marriage was registered
Confirm whether your spouse has left the country through an immigration records inquiry made through the court
Keep records of any missing-person report and messages showing attempts to make contact
If the marriage was a means of entering Korea from the start, also consider annulment of the marriage (혼인무효)

body.text: Conversely, if you obtained a divorce judgment from a foreign court, it must meet the recognition requirements of Article 217 of the Civil Procedure Act before it can be reflected in the Korean family relations register. The points examined are whether that court had international jurisdiction, whether the defendant was lawfully served by a method other than service by public notice or appeared in the proceedings, whether it is contrary to good morals, and whether there is reciprocity. Please also bear in mind that to have a divorce in Korea reflected in the civil status records of your spouse's country, you must separately follow that country's procedures.

author: kim-miso

title: Can you divorce over ‘incompatible personalities’? Rereading Article 840 of the Civil Act
summary: The phrase ‘incompatible personalities’ does not appear in the statute. We set out what each of the six grounds for judicial divorce means, and why the ground you choose determines how you prepare your evidence.

body.text: “Can I get a divorce because of incompatible personalities?” This question often comes up at the start of a consultation. If your spouse does not agree to a divorce, the court looks at whether one of the grounds set out in Article 840 of the Civil Act exists. That provision does not mention incompatible personalities, but that does not mean divorce is blocked.
Five of them are specific grounds
Article 840 lists six grounds. The first five are relatively clear.

items: Item 1, an unchaste act by the spouse: even without sexual intercourse, it may apply if the act betrays the marital duty of fidelity
Item 2, malicious desertion: a typical example is leaving home without a justifiable reason, cutting off living expenses and not returning
Item 3, extremely unjust treatment by the spouse or the spouse's lineal ascendants: unbearable treatment such as violence or severe insults
Item 4, extremely unjust treatment of one's own lineal ascendants by the spouse: verbal abuse or mistreatment directed at your parents
Item 5, where it has been unclear for three years or more whether the spouse is alive or dead

body.text: The sixth ground is the broadest

Item 6 is ‘any other serious reason making it difficult to continue the marriage’. Circumstances that do not fit neatly into the first five, such as incompatible personalities, long separation, a life without communication, financial problems or conflict with in-laws, are mostly dealt with here.

What the court looks at is not the label of the conflict but its result. It considers whether the marriage has broken down to the point where it is hard to restore, and whether being told to continue the marriage would cause one party unbearable suffering. However, if the main responsibility for the breakdown lies with the party seeking the divorce, the matter becomes one of a divorce claim by the spouse at fault (유책배우자), which in principle is not accepted.

The circumstances used in this judgment are specific. How long the separation has lasted, what contact and living expenses were like during that time, whether there were attempts at couples counseling or restoring the relationship, and whether the other spouse has shown through their actions an intention to continue the marriage are all reviewed together. The course of life over several years often carries more weight than one or two big fights. So when relying on item 6, the starting point is a timeline setting out the conflicts since the marriage in date order.
The ground you choose determines the evidence

You do not have to choose just one ground, and in practice several grounds are often argued together. Still, deciding on the central ground determines what materials to gather. For an unchaste act you need messages and payment records; for malicious desertion, account records showing living expenses were cut off; for unjust treatment, medical certificates and records of reports.

You also need to watch the time limits. Under item 1, you can no longer claim on that ground once six months have passed since you learned of it or two years since it occurred (Article 841), and item 6 has the same periods (Article 842). However, case law holds that these periods are not a problem if the broken state of the marriage still continues today. Incompatible personalities is a phrase not found in the statute, but it is no reason you cannot go to court either.

author: kim-miso

title: Choosing the custodial parent: what comes before financial means
summary: Courts decide custody not by which parent was more at fault but by which environment is better for the child. We look at how much weight is given to the primary caregiver, the child's wishes, financial means and gender.

body.text: What parents fighting over custody usually worry about first is money: whether they will lose their child because they earn less than the other parent, or whether being the father puts them at a disadvantage. What the court actually gives weight to lies somewhere a little different.
There is one standard: the child's welfare

Articles 837 and 909 of the Civil Act provide that if the parents cannot agree, the family court decides the custodial parent (양육자) and the person with parental authority (친권자) based on the child's welfare. Who broke up the marriage is a matter for compensation for emotional distress, and is not in itself decisive in deciding custody. This means that even a spouse who had an affair can become the custodial parent if they have taken good care of the child.

Parental authority and custody can be given to different people, but in practice they are often given to the same person. This is because the child's daily life is less disrupted if the parent living with the child can handle matters such as school, hospital visits and opening a bank account on their own. Joint parental authority or joint custody is also legally possible, but since it requires the parents to live nearby and consult often, it is hard to have it accepted in cases with intense conflict.
The circumstances given the most weight

What the court considers most important is who has actually been caring for the child so far, and where and how the child is living now. Courts tend to favor the side where the child's life will be least disrupted, so having been the primary caregiver stands at the center of the judgment.

items: Who has mainly handled taking the child to and from school, meals, hospital visits and school meetings
The child's age and whether siblings can be raised together
Housing and work arrangements after the divorce, and who can help with care
The child's wishes (if the child is 13 or older, the court must in principle hear the child's views)
Problems such as violence, neglect or drinking
An attitude of respecting the child's relationship with the other parent

body.text: Financial means and gender are not decisive

If the parent with less income becomes the custodial parent, this can be made up for by receiving child support from the other parent. So financial means are a factor, but custody is not decided on that alone. Gender is not a standard either. If the father has actually been the main caregiver and shows a plan to raise the child stably after the divorce, he can be designated as the custodial parent.

The child's wishes are given important consideration, but they do not simply become the conclusion. Under Article 100 of the Rules on Family Litigation, the court in principle hears the views of a child aged 13 or older, and even with younger children, their feelings are sometimes explored during the family investigation (가사조사). Signs that a parent pressured the child to choose a side may actually be assessed unfavorably.
The moment separation begins is important

Once separation begins, the care arrangements from that point affect the later judgment. If one parent takes the child and raises them for a long time, that situation can become entrenched, so if you have been separated from your child, do not delay applying for designation of a temporary custodial parent through a preliminary disposition (사전처분). Conversely, taking the child away without the other parent's knowledge may look bad to the court, so be careful.

author: kim-miso

title: The child support table is only a starting point
summary: Child support starts from the standard amount in the calculation table and is set by adding or subtracting for the circumstances of the child and parents. We explain how to read the table, the grounds for increases and reductions, and the question of costs after the child reaches adulthood.

body.text: People looking into child support usually start by finding the Child Support Calculation Table (양육비 산정기준표). Match the bracket for the parents' combined income with the child's age and an amount comes out, so it looks simple. But the amount actually set by the court often differs from the number in the table.
How to read the table

Based on the Child Support Calculation Table published by the Seoul Family Court, the court finds the standard child support amount that matches the parents' combined income and the age and number of children. It then divides this amount according to the ratio of the parents' incomes to set the share to be paid by the parent who does not live with the child. For example, if the two parents earn about the same, roughly half the standard amount is calculated as the non-custodial parent's burden, and if one parent earns much more, a larger share in proportion to that parent's ratio is calculated.

The first point of dispute here is income. For salaried workers it is relatively clear from the withholding tax receipt, but for self-employed people and freelancers, reported income and actual standard of living often differ. In that case, you argue for the actual income to be estimated from card spending records, vehicles and housing, and business sales data, and if necessary you apply for a property disclosure order (재산명시) and a property inquiry (재산조회).
Circumstances that add or subtract
The table's amounts assume an average household, so the court can increase or reduce them depending on the circumstances. The circumstances we often deal with in consultations are these.

items: Where the child needs long-term treatment or has a disability and costs are high
Where the child has been receiving costly education, such as in the arts or sports, consistently since before the divorce
Where the parents have substantial assets relative to their income
Where the paying parent has other family members to support
Where the custodial parent's housing costs are low, for example because they use the home they live in with the child without paying for it

body.text: The side arguing for an increase must show the costs actually spent with receipts and account records, and the side arguing for a reduction must show income and support burdens with documents. Arguments made only in words find it hard to move the numbers in the table.

The calculation also differs depending on the number of children. The amounts in the table are per child and assume a household with two children, and the table also explains how to adjust the amount where there is one child or three or more. Where siblings are raised separately by each parent, the arrangement is sometimes that each parent calculates the share for the child they raise and only the difference is paid.
After adulthood, and later changes

Child support set by the court is in principle for costs until the child reaches adulthood. Costs after adulthood, such as university tuition, can be claimed under an agreement if the parents have made one separately, so if you want this, write down how the costs will be shared in the agreement at the time of divorce.

If circumstances change after the amount is set, you can claim an increase or reduction. The child moving on to a higher level of school, or the paying parent losing their job, can be grounds for this. However, the paying parent must know that if they reduce payments on their own without a court decision, the difference simply builds up as unpaid child support. The number in the table is the starting line for negotiation, and the conclusion is shaped by the evidence.

author: kim-miso

title: ‘Whose name it is in doesn't matter’ is only half right
summary: It is true that title is not decisive in the division of property, but property owned before marriage and property inherited or received as a gift are different. We look at the relationship between Article 830 of the Civil Act and contribution.

body.text: When the division of property comes up, we often hear, “They say it doesn't matter whose name it's in.” It is not wrong, since it means that property built up together during the marriage is subject to division whether it is in the husband's or the wife's name. But applying this to every asset in the same way throws the calculation far off.
The law actually starts from title

Article 830 of the Civil Act defines property one spouse owned before the marriage and property acquired in their own name during the marriage as that spouse's separate property (특유재산). Only property whose ownership is unclear is presumed to be jointly owned by the couple. Looking at the provision alone, title seems quite important.

However, Article 839-2, which governs the division of property, calls for dividing ‘property formed through the cooperation of both parties’. Even an apartment bought in one spouse's name during the marriage becomes property formed through cooperation if the other spouse helped build it through housework and childcare, dual income or loan repayments. This is where the saying that title does not matter comes from.

Conversely, even property bought during the marriage may be excluded from division if one spouse bought it solely with money they had before the marriage and the other played no role in maintaining it. So it is more accurate to understand ‘title doesn't matter’ as meaning ‘title alone does not decide the outcome’. The work of examining the source of funds and contributions still remains.
Property from before the marriage and inherited property

Property owned before the marriage, and property inherited or received as a gift from parents during the marriage, is in principle excluded from division, because it was not formed through cooperation. However, case law holds that if the other spouse contributed to maintaining that property or increasing its value, it can be included in the division.
What is recognized as contribution differs case by case, but the situations we often deal with in consultations are these.

items: Where the loan on a home one spouse bought before marriage was repaid together from both spouses' income after the marriage
Where inherited land was managed together and a building was built on it to earn rental income
Where money from parents became the seed money for the newlyweds' first home, which was then grown through several moves
Where one spouse helped for a long time with bookkeeping and client management for a business in the other spouse's name

body.text: In the end, it is about showing the flow of funds

In cases disputing title, the most powerful evidence is account records showing where money came from and where it went. The side claiming property was owned before the marriage must show when it was acquired and where the funds came from, and the side claiming contribution must show later loan repayments and management records. For money contributed by parents, transfer records and conversations showing to whom the money was given at the time are important.

Money received from both families at the time of the wedding is especially prone to being argued from memory. If the two sides disagree about who contributed how much over a decade ago, bank statements from that time or the source of the down payment in the sale contract decide the outcome. Bank transaction records can often be issued even for periods long ago, so please check in advance before litigation.

The length of the marriage is also considered. If the couple has not been married long, property from before the marriage or gifted property is often excluded from the calculation, but if they have lived together for decades and their assets have become intermingled, it becomes hard to separate the original sources. That is why the same question gets different answers depending on the length of the marriage. Title is the starting point, and the conclusion is reached by who did what for that property.

author: kim-miso

title: The 30 days after receiving a divorce complaint, broken down week by week
summary: The 30-day deadline for an answer looks long, but it passes quickly while you are pulling your emotions together. We set out, in order, how to use the four weeks from the day you receive the complaint.

body.text: On the day the court envelope arrives, most people cannot focus on anything. The picture of themselves in the complaint feels unfamiliar and unfair, and some let several days pass without doing anything. The answer must be filed within 30 days of being served with a copy of the complaint (Article 256 of the Civil Procedure Act and Article 12 of the Family Litigation Act), and once a week or two goes by like that, the remaining time gets tight. Thinking of the 30 days as four weeks makes it feel a little less overwhelming.
Weeks one and two

In the first week, write the date of receipt on the envelope and lay out all the documents that came with it. Besides the complaint, an application for a preliminary disposition (사전처분) or a provisional attachment order (가압류) may have arrived with it, and these need to be dealt with separately. In the claims section, find and mark the amount of compensation for emotional distress, the demands for division of property and the demands concerning the children, and it is a good idea to get a consultation within this week.

In the second week, read the factual allegations in the complaint line by line and sort them into what you admit, what you do not know, and what is untrue. Next to the untrue parts, note where the evidence to rebut them is. Then make the most important decision: whether you do not want the divorce at all, or whether you accept the divorce but will dispute the terms.

If you have children, also review their daily life during this period. If the complaint says the other parent wants to be the custodial parent, gather in advance the materials showing who has been caring for the children so far, so that you are not shaken during the family investigation (가사조사).
Weeks three and four

In the third week, prepare your documents in line with that decision. If you should receive compensation for emotional distress or a division of property, or you want to raise the children, an answer alone is not enough and you need to file a counterclaim as well. If living expenses have been cut off or there is a dispute over the children, consider applying for a preliminary disposition at this point too. If there are signs that the other party is moving assets, it is also wise not to miss this window for a provisional attachment.

In the fourth week, finalize and file your documents. If you have not finished gathering materials, file an answer setting out your basic position first and supplement the rest with preparatory briefs. In a divorce case, not filing an answer does not mean the other party's claims are accepted as they are (proviso to Article 12 of the Family Litigation Act), but in the meantime the court reads only the plaintiff's side of the story first.

The shorter the sentences in the answer, the better. If you rebut every expression in the complaint emotionally, the document gets long and the key points the court needs to see become blurred. It is enough to pick only the parts of the other party's claims that affect the outcome and answer them with facts and evidence, and simply note that you dispute the rest.
What not to do in the meantime

items: Sending the other party long, confrontational messages
Moving savings or disposing of the home
Suddenly moving house with the children
Posting about the lawsuit on social media

body.text: If the case is proceeding through electronic litigation, the other party's filings, hearing notices and orders to make corrections are posted on the website. Make it a habit to check the case history at least once a week. From the moment you receive the complaint, time runs on the court's schedule, not the other party's.

author: kim-miso

title: Can you lose a lawsuit against the affair partner even with clear evidence of the affair?
summary: Even if your spouse's affair is clear, the affair partner's liability is assessed separately. We set out the three requirements the court checks and the gaps that are often left empty.

body.text: “We even have photos of them going into a motel together. Could we still lose?” When we hear this question, we first ask back not about the scene in the photo but about what that person knew. A claim for compensation for emotional distress against an affair partner is not a divorce case but a damages case for a tort under Article 750 of the Civil Act. A tort requires intent or negligence on the part of the person who acted.
Your spouse's wrong and the affair partner's wrong are assessed separately

The fact that your spouse had an affair shows your spouse's wrongdoing. To hold the affair partner liable, there must be a separate wrong attributable to that person. The Supreme Court holds that a third party who commits an unchaste act with one spouse and thereby infringes the couple's shared married life in principle commits a tort, and is jointly liable with the spouse as a joint tortfeasor (Supreme Court Decision 2013Meu2441, May 29, 2015). The words to note here are infringement of the couple's shared married life, and acting with knowledge of it. This is also why you can bring a claim against the affair partner alone without divorcing. Even if the marriage continues, the harm of the infringement of shared married life remains.
The three things the court checks
In practice, courts generally look at three things separately. If even one is missing, the outcome is shaken no matter how much other evidence there is.

items: Whether the two were in a romantic relationship. Even if sexual intercourse cannot be proven, a relationship that breaches the duty of fidelity amounts to an unchaste act.
Whether the affair partner knew, or could have known, that your spouse had a family.
Whether your shared married life was actually continuing at the time.

body.text: In consultations, we often see plenty of material on the first question while the second and third are almost empty. A hotel receipt shows the relationship, but it does not go so far as to show that the affair partner knew your spouse was married.

Case law does not go so far as to impose a duty to check whether a romantic partner has a spouse. So a vague claim that the affair partner could have known carries little force; it needs specific circumstances, such as your spouse always wearing a wedding ring or being out of contact every weekend because of family plans.
How to fill the gaps

Knowledge of the marriage is most often revealed in the two people's conversations. Typical examples are talk about the children, remarks about being careful around the spouse, and pressure to get a divorce. If there are no such conversations, gather indirect material period by period, such as a messenger profile with family photos, or the fact that they met at a workplace or group where the marriage was known.

The fact that the marriage was continuing is surprisingly easy to forget. Ordinary records showing that you lived in the same home, shared living expenses, and spent holidays and children's events together block the other side's claim that the marriage had broken down. The affair partner who claims the marriage had already broken down must prove it (Supreme Court Decision 2022Meu13504, 13511, June 27, 2024), but having rebuttal material ready in advance makes the trial proceed much more steadily.

Before writing the complaint, try sorting the material you have into a three-column table. The empty column is where the other side will attack. As you fill in the table, you may find you have more material than you thought, or you may conclude that you should not file the complaint yet. Either way, that judgment needs to be made before filing.

author: kim-miso

title: What it takes for ‘I didn't know he was married’ to be accepted
summary: If you did not know the person was married, liability as an affair partner may be denied. But saying you did not know is not enough; you also need to show when you found out and what you did afterwards.

body.text: The thing we hear most often from people who have received a complaint as an affair partner is that they did not know. They say they were never told the person was married and that the person seemed to live alone. This argument has legal significance too, because the affair partner's liability is liability in tort, and a tort requires intent or negligence (Article 750 of the Civil Act).
The burden of proof is on the plaintiff to begin with

Case law does not go so far as to impose a duty to check whether a romantic partner has a spouse. So it is the plaintiff bringing the claim who must prove that the affair partner knew, or could have known, of the marriage. On this point alone, it may seem the defendant can simply sit back.

Negligence is examined as well. Even if you did not actually know, liability may be found if there were circumstances from which you could have known with a little care. This is why, between people who worked together on the same team for several years, a claim of not knowing about the marriage is not easily accepted.

Actual trials do not unfold that way. The plaintiff picks out parts of the two people's conversations that mention children or a spouse, and puts forward the fact that they were at the same workplace or in the same group. If the defendant cannot then present specific circumstances to the contrary, the court tends to lean toward the plaintiff's circumstantial evidence. Proof may be the plaintiff's burden, but in the end it is the defendant who must persuade.
The three things the court asks

When examining a claim of not knowing, the court generally seeks to confirm three things: what words and actions deceived you, when you learned of the marriage, and how you acted after finding out. If you have the following materials, set them aside and keep them safe now.

items: Messages in which the other person introduced themselves as single or divorced, and conversations in which you asked whether they were married
Circumstances showing they lived like a single person, such as meeting freely on weekends and holidays and having you visit their home
The date you found out about the marriage and how it happened
Messages right after that in which you cut off contact or protested

body.text: The third question is especially important. If the meetings continued after you found out, liability may be found for the period after that. If you set out the period when you did not know separately from the period when you did, you may not be able to dispute liability entirely, but you can narrow its scope.
Arguments that can backfire

Insisting you did not know when the circumstances from which you could have known are obvious is risky. If a photo with a wedding ring was on the person's profile, or your conversations frequently mention their child's after-school classes, the court will find it hard to believe that argument. Once one argument collapses, the rest lose credibility too.

In such cases, some cases are better served by admitting what should be admitted and putting the weight on the short length of the relationship and the fact that you ended it as soon as it was discovered. Which path to take is decided by looking at the plaintiff's evidence together with the conversations you have. If the other person ever showed you documents claiming to be divorced, be sure to keep those photos or conversations. Also avoid contacting the plaintiff or the other spouse directly to explain yourself after receiving the complaint. Things said in an emotional phone call are sometimes used as an admission that you knew about the marriage.

author: kim-miso

title: The 30 days from receiving an affair lawsuit complaint: how to divide them
summary: The 30-day deadline for an answer looks long, but it passes quickly. We set out, in order and week by week, what a defendant who has received the complaint needs to do.

body.text: The clock starts the moment you tear open the court envelope. The defendant must file an answer within 30 days of receiving a copy of the complaint, and if no answer is filed, the court may treat the plaintiff's claims as admitted and give judgment without a hearing (Articles 256 and 257 of the Civil Procedure Act). If a family member living with you received it on your behalf, that day is the reference point, and the deadline does not get longer because you opened the envelope a few days later. If the 30th day falls on a Saturday or public holiday, the deadline runs to the following day. Dividing the 30 days roughly into three stages makes the tasks easier to see.
Week one: read and preserve

Gather the complaint, the attached evidence, the envelope and the guidance notes in one place. Mark the amount claimed, the period of the relationship the plaintiff alleges, and the grounds on which the plaintiff says you knew of the marriage. The most important thing this week is not to delete your conversations with the other spouse. Records favorable to you, such as messages saying they were single, are in there too.

Sometimes a provisional attachment order (가압류) arrives before or together with the complaint. This means the plaintiff has frozen your deposits or wages before judgment, and the money does not go straight to the plaintiff. If you think the provisional attachment is excessive, you can challenge it by filing an objection (Article 283 of the Civil Execution Act), so keep the order together with the complaint.
Weeks two and three: set the direction

Sort the contents of the complaint into what is true, what is wrong and what is exaggerated. Then decide whether to dispute the unchaste act itself, say you did not know of the marriage, argue the marriage had already broken down at the time, or accept liability and dispute the amount. Whichever you choose, pick only arguments supported by the material you have.

If you intend to argue that the marriage had broken down, keep in mind that the defendant must prove it (Supreme Court Decision 2022Meu13504, 13511, June 27, 2024). Rather than the other spouse's word that ‘we were already finished’, you need objective material such as when the separation began or when a divorce suit was filed.
Week four: file first, supplement later

An answer is usually written in two parts. The first states the conclusion, asking for the plaintiff's claim to be dismissed, and the second sets out which of the plaintiff's allegations you admit and which you dispute, with your reasons and evidence. Evidence is submitted together, numbered as the defendant's exhibits, such as Eul No. 1 (을 제1호증) and Eul No. 2.

If you have not finished gathering material, one approach is to file an answer within the deadline stating that you dispute the claim, and supplement the detailed arguments with preparatory briefs. If an answer is filed before judgment is pronounced, judgment without a hearing will not be given (proviso to Article 257(1) of the Civil Procedure Act), but there is no reason to rely on that proviso and miss the deadline.

There are also principles to keep throughout the 30 days. Messages sent to explain yourself become evidence for the plaintiff, and signs of getting stories straight undermine the credibility of your whole account.

items: Do not contact the plaintiff or the other spouse to explain yourself
Do not coordinate your account with the other spouse
Do not pour out the story of the case to people around you

author: kim-miso

title: Inheritance with family members of foreign nationality: which country's law applies?
summary: Even if an heir has foreign nationality, the Korean Civil Act is the standard if the deceased was a Korean national. We set out the principle and exceptions for deciding the applicable law, the validity of wills made abroad, and documents and deadlines for heirs overseas.

body.text: As more siblings have emigrated, it has become common for some heirs to be foreign citizens. The first question in such cases is, “My younger brother is a U.S. citizen. Can he still inherit?” He can. This is because the standard for deciding the law applicable to inheritance lies with the deceased, not the heir.
The deceased's nationality is the standard

Article 77(1) of the Act on Private International Law (국제사법) provides that inheritance is governed by the law of the deceased's nationality at the time of death. If your parents died as Korean nationals, the heirs and their shares are decided under the Korean Civil Act whether an heir is a U.S. citizen or lives in Japan, and an heir's nationality does not change their share.

Conversely, if a father who acquired foreign nationality died leaving land in Korea, the law of that country is the standard in principle. However, if that country's law in turn provides for Korean law to apply, Korean law may govern (Article 22 of the Act on Private International Law), and if the deceased expressly designated in a will the law of their habitual residence or the law of the place where the real estate is located, that law applies (Article 77(2)). This is why the conclusion can differ from case to case even for the same land.
Wills written abroad

The rules on the form of a will are generous. It is enough for the will to comply with any one of the following: the law of a country of which the testator was a national at the time of making the will or at death, the law of the testator's habitual residence at the time of making the will or at death, the law of the place where the will was made, or, for a will concerning real estate, the law of the place where it is located (Article 78(3)). This means a will made in the United States in the local form can also be valid in Korea. However, registering property in Korea on the basis of that will may separately require procedures such as probate (검인) or translation and authentication.
Deadlines run the same way abroad

The three-month period for renunciation of inheritance (상속포기) and qualified acceptance (한정승인) runs just the same even if you are abroad. Korean nationals residing abroad can obtain signature authentication at a Korean diplomatic mission in place of a certificate of seal impression, while foreign nationals need local notarization, an apostille or consular confirmation, and a translation. Authentication can take several weeks, so we also consider appointing a domestic agent by power of attorney or requesting an extension of the period.

items: If an heir has an address abroad, the filing deadline for acquisition tax and inheritance tax is extended to nine months (Article 20 of the Local Tax Act and Article 67 of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act).

A foreign national who acquires real estate in Korea through inheritance must report it to the competent authority within six months of acquisition (Article 8(2) of the Act on Report on Real Estate Transactions).
Preparing in advance documents linking your Korean name with the name in your foreign passport as the same person can reduce requests for corrections.

body.text: For assets located abroad, even if the shares are determined under Korean law, separate procedures with the courts or authorities of that country are often required. Saving time and cost starts with making a table of which assets are in which country and how much, and deciding which country's procedures to go through first. So that domestic deadlines do not pass while heirs living abroad are slow to respond to discussions, set the order of tasks starting with those that have deadlines.

author: kim-miso

title: The order in which inheritance documents travel when a sibling lives abroad
summary: When one of the heirs lives abroad, even a single signature can take several weeks. Here is how to plan a schedule that covers the documents needed for each nationality without missing deadlines.

body.text: Families with an older sister living in the United States or a younger brother who emigrated to Canada stall at some point in the inheritance process. Getting a seal on a single division agreement takes a day or two in Korea, but from abroad it can take several weeks because of consulate appointments and international mail. Yet inheritance deadlines are not delayed because someone is overseas. This is why you need to put the fact that a sibling lives abroad at the center of your schedule from the start.
Check nationality first

For Korean nationals residing abroad who have kept their Korean nationality, a common method is to have their signature on the division agreement or power of attorney authenticated at a Korean diplomatic mission in their country of residence, in place of a certificate of seal impression (인감증명서). If they have changed to a foreign nationality, they need local notarization and an apostille or consular confirmation, plus a translation, and must also prepare documents linking their Korean name with the name in their foreign passport as the same person.

Either way, an heir's nationality does not change the right of inheritance itself. The inheritance of parents who were Korean nationals follows the Korean Civil Act, and a sibling of foreign nationality is equally an heir. The only thing that differs is how the documents are prepared. Notarization methods and whether a country is party to the Apostille Convention vary, so checking and passing on the procedures of the country where your sibling lives first can save wasted trips.
Count the deadlines backwards

items: Renunciation of inheritance (상속포기) and qualified acceptance (한정승인): three months from the day you learned; the period runs the same way abroad
Inheritance tax and acquisition tax returns: nine months if an heir has an address abroad
A foreign national who acquires real estate in Korea through inheritance must report it within six months of acquisition
Build the several weeks needed for document authentication and international mail into the schedule in advance

body.text: Especially if renunciation of inheritance is needed, contact your sibling abroad first. A commonly used method is to appoint a domestic agent with an authenticated power of attorney to file with the family court, but obtaining even one power of attorney takes time. If the decision looks like it will be delayed, consider requesting an extension of the period before the three months run out.
Decide which documents to get in one go and send them together

The most common mistake is requesting documents several times in separate batches. If, after getting a signature on the division agreement, a power of attorney for the bank is needed, and then documents for registration, your sibling abroad grows weary and the time doubles. It is better to put together everything needed, such as the division agreement, powers of attorney and identity confirmation documents, and send it all at once with a checklist.

Explain the contents of the division agreement thoroughly by email before it is signed. If phone calls are difficult because of the time difference, sending the list of assets and the calculation table as files and answering questions as they come actually leaves a record and causes fewer misunderstandings. The farther away a sibling is and the less they know of the situation, the more likely they are to say later that they did not know. If the deceased had foreign nationality or left bank accounts or a house abroad, which country's law and procedures to follow must first be reviewed separately, so if that applies, please let us know at the start of the consultation.

author: kim-miso

title: The three months for renouncing an inheritance do not run from the date of death
summary: The three months for renunciation and qualified acceptance are counted not from the date of death but from the day you learned that the inheritance had begun and that you had become an heir. For family members who heard the news late and for lower-ranking heirs, the starting point is different.

body.text: Ask about the deadline for renouncing an inheritance and most people say three months from the date of death. That is not wrong, but it is not precise either. Article 1019(1) of the Civil Act sets the starting point as ‘the day one learned that the inheritance had commenced’, and courts read this as the day one learned both that the deceased had died and that one had thereby become an heir.
A child at the deathbed and a child who heard the news late

For a child who was at their parent's side when they died, the date of death and the day they learned are the same, so you count from that day. On the other hand, for a child who received news by post several months later that a father they had long been out of touch with had died, the day they heard the news can be the starting point. However, courts usually assume you knew on the date of death, so the person filing must show the circumstances of learning late. Do not throw away the text message or the registered mail envelope through which you were informed.
From when do lower-ranking heirs count?

Sometimes all the children renounce and grandchildren or siblings become the heirs. In that case, Supreme Court case law holds that the three months for a lower-ranking heir run from the day they learned that the higher-ranking heirs had renounced and that they had become an heir as a result. Writing down the day you heard your older brother had renounced, or the day you first received a demand from a creditor, gives you a basis if the starting point is disputed later.

When it goes down to the fourth rank, cousins who had little contact with the deceased can become heirs. They are not eligible to apply for the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service (안심상속 원스톱서비스), so they must check the assets and debts separately through the Financial Supervisory Service's inquiry into heirs' financial transactions. It takes time for the results to come back, so it is a good idea to consider requesting an extension of the period at the same time.
Learning of the debts late is a different matter

Some people think that if they knew of the death and that they had become an heir but did not know there were debts, the three months start again from when they found out. That is not so. The original three months have already run, and if you did not know, without gross negligence, that the debts exceeded the assets, you must turn to special qualified acceptance (특별한정승인), made within three months of learning that fact (paragraph (3) of the same Article). On this route, renunciation is not available; only qualified acceptance is possible.

items: If it is hard to decide because the asset inquiries are not finished, you can request an extension of the period from the family court before the three months pass.
It is enough for the filing to be received within the three months; the court's decision accepting it does not have to come out within that time.
If an heir is a minor, the period is counted from the day the person with parental authority or the guardian learned that the inheritance had commenced (Article 1020 of the Civil Act).

body.text: Calculating the final day is also more confusing than you might think. The Civil Act does not count the first day of a period and starts from the next day (Article 157), and a period in months is reckoned by the calendar and ends on the day before the day in the last month corresponding to the starting day (Article 160). If you learned on March 10, June 10 is the last day, and if that day is a Saturday or public holiday, it is extended to the next day (Article 161). Even so, we do not recommend filing on the last day, because it is common for one document to be missing and need to be obtained again.
A single date can decide the outcome. If the starting point is unclear, it is safer to take the earliest possible date as your reference and act on it.

author: kim-miso

title: Why touching the deceased's property can block renunciation of inheritance
summary: If you dispose of inherited property, the law treats you as having accepted the inheritance. Using the provisions on statutory simple acceptance, we look at which actions count as disposal and what to be careful about even after renouncing.

body.text: The Civil Act has a provision that treats an heir as having accepted the inheritance regardless of what they actually intended. This is statutory simple acceptance (법정단순승인) under Article 1026. If you fall under it, renunciation of inheritance (상속포기) or qualified acceptance (한정승인) may not be accepted even if the debts far exceed the assets. This is also why something done without thinking while arranging the funeral can become a problem months later.
Three cases the law treats as simple acceptance

items: When the heir has disposed of inherited property (item 1)
When the heir has not made a qualified acceptance or renunciation within three months (item 2)
When, after a qualified acceptance or renunciation, the heir has concealed inherited property, used it up improperly, or deliberately left it out of the inventory of assets (item 3)

body.text: What counts as disposal

Typical examples are withdrawing the deceased's deposits and using them for living expenses, selling the deceased's car or transferring it into your name, and collecting a lease deposit owed back to the deceased and splitting it among siblings. There is case law holding that paying costs within a socially reasonable range, such as funeral expenses, from inherited property is not disposal, but you must be able to explain the amount and use with receipts. Even for funeral expenses, the judgment may differ if the amount was excessive or leftover money was used personally.
