From September 11, 2026, financial transactions in the deceased's name are blocked from the day after the death is reported. For urgent funeral and hospital expenses, using the exceptional withdrawal by which the financial institution pays the hospital or funeral home directly means the money does not pass through the heirs' hands, which also reduces disputes over disposal.

Conversely, some money looks like disposal but is not. Death insurance payouts naming a spouse or child as beneficiary, and benefits for which the law designates the recipient, such as National Pension survivors' pensions, are not inherited property but the recipient's own property, so in principle receiving them does not amount to simple acceptance. However, if the deceased is named as the insurance beneficiary, that payout is inherited property, so check the policy first.

In fact, the most common form of simple acceptance is item 2. If three months pass without any filing, it simply becomes simple acceptance. It is not unusual for people to miss the deadline while waiting for the results of asset inquiries, so if the results are delayed, it is safer to request an extension before the period ends.
It is not over even after you renounce

Item 3 applies after a renunciation or qualified acceptance has been accepted. If you quietly took jewelry or cash from the deceased's home, or left a deposit you knew about out of the inventory for a qualified acceptance, it may be treated as simple acceptance. A person who has renounced must also continue to manage the property with the same care as their own until the person who became an heir through that renunciation is able to manage it (Article 1044).

If you have already moved money out of the deceased's account, it is better to set out when, how much and on what it was spent than to hide it. Whether it was disposal or not is ultimately judged by looking at that record. If any cash remains, keep it separately, and collect the receipts for money spent, sorted by funeral home and hospital.

author: kim-miso

title: The legal weight of “I'll pay you once the next tenant moves in”
summary: A new tenant moving in is not a condition for returning the deposit. However, you need to sort out the simultaneous performance relationship and the date the lease ended before you can hold the landlord responsible.

body.text: This is probably the sentence tenants hear most often from landlords a month or two before the lease expires, and even more so when the jeonse (전세) market has frozen. But the law attaches no such condition to the return of the deposit.
Returning the deposit and vacating the home are linked

When a lease ends, the landlord must return the deposit and the tenant must vacate the home. The two obligations are to be performed simultaneously. Finding a new tenant is only the landlord's own concern, not a condition that triggers the obligation to return the deposit. Even after the lease term ends, the lease relationship is deemed to continue until the deposit is returned (Article 4(2) of the Housing Lease Protection Act (주택임대차보호법)), so the tenant's status is also maintained in the meantime.

The simultaneous performance relationship leaves the tenant with homework too. If the tenant keeps living there without preparing to vacate, it is hard to hold the landlord responsible for the delay in returning the deposit. That is why you need to plan when to move and which procedures to follow together.
The first thing to examine is whether the lease has ended

Surprisingly, the first issue in deposit disputes is the end date. If the landlord does not give notice of non-renewal between six months and two months before expiry, or the tenant does not do so by two months before expiry, the lease is deemed renewed on the same terms (Article 6 of the same Act). After such an implied renewal, the tenant may give notice of termination at any time, and it takes effect three months after the landlord receives the notice (Article 6-2 of the same Act).

Where the landlord did not refuse renewal and the lease was renewed because the tenant exercised the right to request renewal of the contract (계약갱신요구권), the tenant may likewise give notice of termination at any time, and it likewise takes effect three months later. In the end, the end date can only be calculated accurately by checking how the renewal came about and when the notice reached the other party.

If you only said verbally that you would move out, a dispute may later arise over whether notice was given. Please give notice by a method that leaves a date on record, such as a text message or certified mail (내용증명).
If your moving date is fixed

If you have to move without getting your deposit back, apply for a lease registration order (임차권등기명령), confirm that the lease registration appears on the certificate of registered matters, and only then move your belongings out and transfer your resident registration. Once registered, your opposability and priority right to repayment are preserved, and you can claim the costs of the application and registration from the landlord (Article 3-3 of the same Act). Moving your resident registration when you have only applied is risky.

You can only apply for registration after the lease has ended. If you gave notice of termination after an implied renewal, you can apply once three months have passed, so it is safer to count backwards from the move-in date of your new home to decide when to give notice.
Waiting for a new tenant is a choice, not an obligation. If you decide to wait, it is a good idea to put in writing how long you will wait and what will happen if the deposit is not returned by then.

author: park-jongjin

title: If your moving day is approaching but the lease registration has not come through
summary: The balance payment date for your new home is fixed, your deposit has not been returned, and the lease registration is not yet on the register. We set out, in chronological order, what to do first.

body.text: The most nerve-racking moment in a deposit dispute is when the moving date and the registration date do not line up. You have signed the contract for your new home and the balance payment date is set, but the lease registration for the home you live in now has not yet appeared on the register. If you move your belongings out and transfer your move-in report at this point, you may lose your opposability and priority right to repayment, so keeping to the right order matters above all.
The reference point is when it is entered in the register

You can apply for a lease registration order (임차권등기명령) when the lease has ended and you have not received your deposit (Article 3-3(1) of the Housing Lease Protection Act (주택임대차보호법)), and once registration is made, the opposability and priority right to repayment you already have are preserved even if you move (paragraph (5) of the same Article). The reference point is neither the day you applied nor the day the order was issued, but the time the lease registration is entered in the register.

Obtain the register from the Internet Registry Office and check for yourself that the housing lease appears in section B (을구). It is easy to assume you can move once you have received the court's order, but it can take more time after the order for the registration to be entered. It is safest to pull the register once more on the morning of moving day.
What you can try when the schedules clash

items: Apply the day after the lease ends, and respond to any court request for corrections the same day
Discuss in advance whether the balance payment or move-in date for your new home can be pushed back a few days
Inform the bank holding your jeonse loan and the guarantee insurer of your schedule and check which documents they need
Do not move out all your belongings or transfer your resident registration before confirming the registration

body.text: You can save time by preparing the application before the lease ends and filing it as soon as the end date passes. Having the lease contract, an abstract of your resident registration, and the text message or certified mail notifying the landlord of the end of the lease ready in advance reduces time lost to corrections. If you apply through electronic litigation, you can check progress online. If the court contacts you about corrections, do not put it off until the next day.

You may hear that it is fine to move as long as you leave some belongings behind, but there is no assurance that this will be recognized as possession. If adjusting the schedule for your new home is truly difficult, please tell us about it at the start of the consultation. We need to work out together the order with the least risk given the remaining dates.

If you have taken out a jeonse deposit return guarantee, also go through the procedure of claiming performance from the guarantor. Each guarantor has its own required documents and order of steps, and many require a register showing the completed lease registration, so ask in advance.
Work remains even after registration

Lease registration is only a device to protect your deposit; it does not return the money. After moving, you obtain an enforceable title through a payment order (지급명령) or a lawsuit for return of the deposit, and if the landlord still does not pay, you apply for a compulsory auction of that home. A lawsuit for return of a deposit proceeds relatively quickly because some of the small claims procedures apply to it regardless of the amount (Article 13 of the Housing Lease Protection Act).

From the day after you vacate the home, you can also claim damages for late payment on the deposit, so keep a record of the date you handed over the keys. You can claim from the landlord the costs of applying for the lease registration order and of registration (Article 3-3(8)). A home with a lease registration becomes hard to rent to a new tenant, so around this time some landlords raise the money and get in touch.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: When there is a record of the transfer but the other person says the money was a gift
summary: In a lawsuit to recover a loan, what the plaintiff must prove is not the transfer but the agreement to repay. We set out what courts look at to distinguish a loan from a gift when there is no IOU.

body.text: The record of sending the money is right there in your bank statement. But once the lawsuit begins, the other person almost always responds with one sentence: it was not a loan, it was money they were given. Many people pour out their sense of injustice when they hear this, but what matters in court is not injustice but proof.
Sending money and lending money are different facts

The Civil Act defines a loan for consumption (소비대차) as a contract in which ownership of money is transferred and the parties agree that the same amount will be returned (Article 598 of the Civil Act). What the party claiming repayment must prove is not the transfer itself but the agreement to repay. A bank transfer record shows only that money passed from one person to another; it does not say whether that money was a loan, a gift or an investment.

So in cases without an IOU, the circumstances before and after the transfer decide the outcome. Points such as whether the message asking for money said ‘I'll pay you back by next month’, and whether the other person, when pressed, replied ‘Please wait a little longer.’ If they did not counter that it was a gift when asked to repay, that reaction is also a relevant circumstance.

Just because the other person claims it was a gift does not mean the plaintiff must disprove a gift without leaving any gaps. However, the judgment differs depending on how many circumstances supporting a loan you put forward, and how specific they are. If you match the transfer records and conversations in a single table in date order before the lawsuit, you can see where the gaps are.
Circumstances the court considers together

items: The relationship between the two people, and whether the amount is a natural one to give as a gift in that relationship
Conversations around the time the money was sent, especially about its purpose and when it would be repaid
Records of any partial repayment or money received as interest
How the other person reacted when asked to repay

body.text: The closer the relationship, such as partners or family, the more easily a gift claim gains weight, especially for living expenses or shared costs. Conversely, if a large sum was sent at once, the judgment may lean toward it being hard to see as given for nothing. Keep in mind that no single circumstance decides the outcome; the court weighs several circumstances together.
Evidence you can still create now

Even if the relationship has already soured, it is sometimes not too late. Send a message stating the amount lent and the date and asking when they can repay, and keep their reply. If the other person does not deny the amount and only talks about when they will repay, that reply can be as good as an IOU. Call recordings can also be used, but they must be recorded by someone who took part in the conversation directly.

There are also points to be careful about. If, in an emotional message, you use an expression that could be read as a gift, such as ‘the money I helped you with back then’, the other person will submit that very sentence as evidence. Read it once more before sending, and if the dispute looks likely to be serious, it is better to seek advice first on how to word your question.

author: park-jongjin

title: What happens if you do not accept registered mail from the court
summary: It may seem that avoiding court mail will stop the case, but in reality it does not. We set out how service is carried out and how deadlines run once you have received documents.

body.text: When a notice of court mail is stuck on your front door, it is frightening. Some people let the post office's holding period lapse, thinking the trial will not start if they do not accept it. But in civil litigation, avoiding service only delays things a little, and in the end it often works to reduce your chance to make your case, because the plaintiff is taking the next steps even while you avoid service.
Service can be made even if you do not accept it

Court documents are in principle handed to the person themselves, but if the person cannot be found at home, they can be handed to a family member living with them (Article 186(1) of the Civil Procedure Act). In principle, the day a family member receives it becomes the day of service, so if a family member takes the mail and passes it on a few days later, your deadline shrinks by that much. If you refuse to accept it without a justifiable reason, service can also be made by leaving the documents at that place (paragraph (3) of the same Article).

If service keeps failing, the plaintiff applies for service at night or on holidays, and if that also fails, the trial proceeds by service by public notice (공시송달). If it proceeds by service by public notice, judgment can be given without the defendant having said a word. Some people only learn there was a lawsuit after their bank account is seized on the basis of that judgment, and to challenge it from that point they must go through procedures with strict requirements, such as a subsequently supplemented appeal (추후보완항소).
Deadlines are counted from the day after receipt
If you have received documents, check the title first. Each document has a different deadline.

items: Payment order (지급명령) or recommendation for performance (이행권고결정): file an objection within two weeks of service
Recommendation for settlement (화해권고결정) or a decision in lieu of conciliation: file an objection within two weeks
Copy of a complaint: file an answer within 30 days
Written judgment: appeal within two weeks

body.text: The period is counted from the day after receipt, and if the last day is a Saturday or public holiday, it runs to the following day (Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Act and Articles 157 and 161 of the Civil Act). Write the last day in large letters on your calendar and, if possible, file a few days early. If you file through electronic litigation, the time of receipt is recorded immediately. If you file by post, the day it arrives at the court is what counts, so mailing it on the last day may be too late.
If you have moved, you must inform the court

If you move while a lawsuit is in progress, you must report your new address to the court immediately (Article 185(1) of the Civil Procedure Act). If you do not, the court may send documents to your old address (paragraph (2) of the same Article), and the fact that you did not receive them is hard to have protected. Even if no lawsuit has started yet, if there is someone you are in a dispute with, it is a good idea to arrange a way to check mail sent to your old address after you move. Applying for the post office's mail forwarding service is one option.

If you have received mail, take a photo of the first page of the documents and the envelope with your phone before putting them in a drawer. These two things are what we check first in a consultation. If the date stamped on the envelope differs from the date you actually received it, do not forget to note the date of receipt separately.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: What people miss when submitting KakaoTalk chats as evidence
summary: Messenger conversations are the most common evidence in civil litigation. We set out how much to capture, keeping the originals, exporting chats, and what to do before changing your phone.

body.text: In cases where money was lent without an IOU, the key evidence showing the loan is usually a messenger conversation. A single line saying they will definitely repay by the end of next month, or will pay a certain amount of interest each month, serves as the contract. That is why how you keep the conversations and how you submit them can decide the outcome.
Capture the context before and after

If you capture only a single favorable line, the other side will produce the surrounding conversation and argue that it meant something else. Captures should show the other person's name or number and the date dividers, and should include plenty of the conversation before and after the sentence in question. Even if parts that look unfavorable are mixed in, deliberately leaving them out actually invites doubts about credibility.

If the conversation is long, also save a text file using KakaoTalk's export chat function. Captures are what you submit to the court, and the exported file is used to show the original flow if the other side claims tampering. It is also a good idea to separately save materials within the chat room, such as voice messages, photos and transfer notifications. If you use a cloud backup, note down the backup date and account as well.

The same principles apply to text messages, Telegram and Instagram messages. If the other person deletes their account or leaves the chat room, the information on your screen may change too, so save everything as soon as there are signs that a dispute is starting.
Before changing your phone

If you are considering a lawsuit, it is better to put off replacing or resetting your phone. Even with a backup, photos or voice messages sometimes go missing during restoration. If you really must change it, back up the chat rooms, export the files and take captures, and keep the old device rather than throwing it away.

If the content of a call matters, a recording of a call you took part in can be submitted as evidence. Keep the original recording file exactly as first recorded, and submit a transcript to the court along with it. If only an edited file remains, a dispute arises over whether it is the original.

items: A screen showing the other person's profile and phone number
Captures showing the date dividers
The exported chat text file
Transfer records supporting the content of the conversation
Your old phone

body.text: If the other side claims tampering

If the other side argues that the captures were edited, reinforce them with other materials that match the conversation, such as transfer records from the same period. Since the same conversation should also remain on the other person's phone, we also consider applying for a document production order (문서제출명령). Even words the other person erased with the message deletion function can be used as evidence if you took a capture before that. If authenticity is seriously disputed, forensic examination may be needed, but it takes time and money.

With evidence, it is less a matter of the more the better than of pinpointing the disputed facts accurately. Rather than submitting hundreds of pages of conversation as they are, pick out and mark the important parts, and organize the rest in date order so it can be submitted when needed. What the court reads is often just the few lines that are marked.

title: Money sent by mistake: you claim it from the recipient, not the bank
summary: In a mistaken transfer, the recipient acquires the deposit claim, so the sender must claim return of unjust enrichment from the recipient, not the bank. We distinguish the scope and order of recovery, and cases that are not mistaken transfers.

body.text: When money goes to a stranger because you mistyped one digit of an account number, the first thing you do is call the bank. The bank may ask the recipient to return it, but if the recipient does not agree, the bank cannot reverse the money on its own. This is because, legally, the party you must ask to return the money is not the bank.
How the legal relationship works

Supreme Court case law holds that once an account transfer is made, the recipient acquires a deposit claim against the bank for that amount, and the sender must claim return of unjust enrichment (부당이득반환) from the recipient (Supreme Court Decision 2007Da51239, November 29, 2007). Even if the transfer was a mistake, you have no right to demand that the bank return the money.

Article 741 of the Civil Act requires a person who, without legal cause, has obtained a benefit from another's property and thereby caused that other a loss to return the benefit. Money that came in by mistake must be returned because the recipient has no legal cause to keep it.
The scope of what you get back

If the recipient received it without knowing the circumstances, they must return it to the extent the benefit remains; if they received it knowingly, they must return the benefit with interest and compensate any loss (Article 748 of the Civil Act). That is why it is a good idea to notify the recipient by message or certified mail (내용증명) that the money was sent by mistake. With money, the benefit is often regarded as remaining even if the recipient has spent it.

A recipient who spends money knowing it came in by mistake may also face criminal liability. When told of this, quite a few recipients get in touch and return the money. If the recipient's account has already been seized by another creditor, matters become complicated, so it is important to act quickly.

Sometimes a recipient says they will return the money but asks for a fee or a reward. Since it is money they are obliged to return, there is no legal reason to agree to such demands; at most you settle actual costs such as the transfer fee.
What to do, in order, if they do not return it

First ask the bank you sent it from to request return of the mistaken transfer, and if you still cannot get it back, move on to the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation's return assistance program, a payment order (지급명령) or a lawsuit. Even if you know only the name and account number, you can file a lawsuit and then apply for a fact inquiry to the bank to find the recipient's address. If the claim is 30 million won or less, it proceeds as a small claims case. A claim for return of unjust enrichment is an ordinary civil claim and is in principle subject to a ten-year limitation period.
Cases that are not mistaken transfers

Money sent after being deceived by voice phishing is not eligible for mistaken transfer return assistance. In that case, immediately ask the sending bank or the receiving bank to suspend payment and report it to the police to start the damage relief procedure. Also, money paid while knowing you owed nothing cannot be reclaimed (Article 742 of the Civil Act), so if you sent the same payment twice, keep evidence that it was a mistake. Please also note that money given for an illegal cause, such as a gambling debt, cannot in principle be recovered (Article 746 of the Civil Act).

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: The table to make first when you receive a summons from the labor office
summary: If you have been summoned by a labor inspector over a former employee's wage arrears petition, start by sorting out the amounts. We also cover the penalties that change from October 8, 2026.

body.text: When a former employee files a petition with the labor office, the employer receives a summons. The moment it arrives, you feel offended, wondering whether you have become a criminal, and want to call the employee to have it out. It is better not to make that call, because it may look like pressure to withdraw the petition. Use that time instead to make a single table.
What you owe and what you paid, side by side

What the labor inspector checks is, in the end, numbers. They will ask in turn about the wage structure in the employment contract, the actual working hours and the amounts already paid. If you make a table of what should have been paid and what was actually paid for each period, and separate the amounts you accept from those you dispute, the investigation becomes much smoother.

items: Employment contract and wage statements
Salary transfer records
Clock-in and clock-out records, access records, POS login records
Time stamps in work messenger apps

body.text: If you are disputing overtime hours, you must respond with objective records, not memory. If the employer only says, “They never worked that late,” the matter is easily settled according to the employee's claims. If you rely on a comprehensive wage agreement (포괄임금 약정), we also look at how that agreement is written in the employment contract.

Making the table sometimes reveals amounts the company had not thought of. Typical examples are annual leave allowances and allowances left out of the severance pay calculation. If you pay the parts you accept first and leave only the parts you dispute, the tone of the investigation changes.

Many employers talk at length in front of the inspector about the employee's attitude or how they left. The hurt feelings are understandable, but they have nothing to do with whether wages are in arrears and do not help the investigation. It is better to say less and answer with the table and records.
How a petition case proceeds

If arrears are confirmed, the inspector orders payment by a set deadline. If you pay within that time, the matter usually ends as an administrative procedure, but if you do not, it turns into a criminal case, and the employer may be questioned as a suspect and referred to the prosecution. Failing to comply with a summons can also lead to an administrative fine (Article 116(2) of the Labor Standards Act (근로기준법)), so if the date does not work, call to ask for it to be rescheduled.

Wages for an employee who has left must be paid within 14 days of departure, after which late payment interest of 20 percent per year applies. This means the longer the investigation drags on, the more you will have to pay.
What changes from October 8

From October 8, 2026, the statutory penalty for wage and severance arrears rises to imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to 50 million won (Article 107 of the Labor Standards Act). For arrears arising before then, the standard is the statutory penalty at the time of the act: imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to 30 million won. The structure under which no indictment can be filed once the affected employee states that they do not want the employer punished is maintained, but there is an exception for employers whose names have been publicly disclosed for wage arrears and who fall into arrears again during the disclosure period.

That is why, in practice, many settlements combine payment with obtaining the employee's statement that they do not want the employer punished (처벌불원). The settlement agreement states the amount and date of payment, the date of each installment if paid in installments, and the wording that the employee does not want punishment. Showing a payment plan first, rather than asking for the statement of non-punishment first, works better in the end.

author: park-jongjin

title: The first week after a workplace harassment report comes in
summary: A company that receives a report must investigate without delay and protect the employee who reported. We set out why it is risky for the CEO to broker a reconciliation, and the order of steps in the first week.

body.text: When a harassment report comes in at a small company, the CEO is tempted to call the two people in and have them clear up the misunderstanding. After all, they know each other and have to keep working together. But what the law requires of the company is not brokering a reconciliation; it is investigation and protection. If you get the order wrong, the company will later be told it failed to fulfill its obligations.
What the law requires

When an employer receives a report or becomes aware of harassment, it must without delay conduct an objective investigation of the parties and others involved (Article 76-3 of the Labor Standards Act (근로기준법)). During the investigation, the employee claiming harm must be protected, but no measure may be taken against that employee's wishes. If harassment is confirmed, the employer must take measures such as a change of workplace at the victim's request, and must hear the victim's views before disciplining the perpetrator.

Unfavorable treatment of the reporter or victim, such as dismissal, is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to 30 million won (Article 109). Failing to investigate or breaching the duty to take measures may lead to an administrative fine, and if the employer personally committed the harassment, an administrative fine of up to 10 million won applies (Article 116). For sexual harassment, the Equal Employment Opportunity Act (남녀고용평등법) sets out investigation and protection in a similar structure.
What to do in the first week

items: Record the date, time and content of the report in writing and inform the reporter that it has been received
Ask the employee claiming harm for their views and decide on protective measures such as separating seating or paid leave
Appoint an investigator with no stake in the matter involving the person accused
Preserve materials that could be deleted, such as messenger chats, emails and CCTV footage
Inform everyone involved in the investigation of their duty of confidentiality

body.text: The investigation starts by breaking down the report into individual acts. If there are two acts, such as verbal abuse and unfair exclusion from work, check separately for each when and where it happened and who saw it. Interview the reporter, the accused and witnesses in that order, and have each person sign their statement.

The investigation report states, act by act, whether it is found to be true and on what basis, and the judgment on whether it went beyond the appropriate scope of work. Even if the conclusion is that harassment is not established, the record of a diligent investigation itself protects the company in any later petition or lawsuit.

Warn the parties in advance not to contact each other or ask witnesses to give statements during the investigation. If there are signs of this, record them with the dates. If the investigation drags on, the anxiety of the employee claiming harm also grows, so letting them know the rough timeline is itself one of the protective measures.
If the person accused is the CEO or an executive

If the person accused directs the investigation, it will be hard to have its objectivity accepted whatever the conclusion. In such cases, it is better to entrust it to an outside investigator and separate the reporting line as well. Even if the investigation does not find harassment, disciplining the reporter calls for great caution unless they made a report they knew to be clearly false.

The harassment provisions of the Labor Standards Act do not apply to workplaces with four or fewer regular employees. Even so, verbal abuse or sexual harassment can lead to criminal or civil liability, so it is not something to take lightly.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: Employee wages when winding up a company: the 2026 substitute payment scope has widened
summary: In bankruptcy and rehabilitation, employee wages are paid before other debts, and if the company has no money, employees can claim substitute payments. Under the amendment that took effect on August 20, 2026, the wage coverage has increased to the final six months.

body.text: What weighs most heavily on a CEO winding up a company is usually the salaries left unpaid to employees. Many people considering corporate bankruptcy or rehabilitation put off the decision because of their employees. From the employees' point of view, however, the company entering court proceedings sometimes actually opens the way to receiving their unpaid wages.
Wages stand ahead of other debts

In bankruptcy proceedings, employees' wages, severance pay and accident compensation are estate claims (재단채권), paid from the bankruptcy estate from time to time and ahead of ordinary bankruptcy claims (Article 473, item 10 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act (채무자 회생 및 파산에 관한 법률)). In rehabilitation proceedings, they are common-benefit claims (공익채권) and must be paid first, from time to time, regardless of the rehabilitation plan (Article 179(1)10). If any company assets remain, the employees' share comes first.
Substitute payments when the company has no money

Even if the company's assets fall short, there is a way. If a decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings or a declaration of bankruptcy has been made against the employer, or the Minister of Employment and Labor has recognized the fact of insolvency, employees who have left can claim substitute payments (대지급금) from the Ministry of Employment and Labor for unpaid wages and the like (Article 7(1) of the Wage Claim Guarantee Act (임금채권보장법)).

This scope widened this year. The Wage Claim Guarantee Act, amended on February 19, 2026 and in force from August 20, 2026, sets substitute payments through this route at the final six months of wages, the final three years of retirement benefits, and the final six months of leave allowances and maternity leave pay (Article 7(2)1). For wages, this is up from the final three months previously. Article 2 of the Addenda provides that it applies to cases where the decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings, the declaration of bankruptcy or the recognition of insolvency is made after it takes effect, so the reference point is not the day the employee left but the day the decision concerning the company was made.

However, substitute payments are subject to a cap set by Presidential Decree, so they may not cover the full amount in arrears. You also need to distinguish this from the other route, through a judgment or a confirmation of unpaid wages, whose scope is set separately. When explaining to employees, mentioning this difference as well reduces misunderstandings.

The provision covers employees who have left. If the company is saved through rehabilitation, the back wages of employees who continue working are common-benefit claims that the company must pay off, and if the company is being wound up, employees are informed of both the timing of their departure and how to claim substitute payments. Either way, a calculation table for each employee must come first.
What the CEO also needs to consider

Wage arrears can lead to criminal issues for the CEO personally. Criminal proceedings over wage arrears do not stop automatically because the corporation is wound up, so the schedule for winding up the corporation and the plan for settling with employees must be drawn up together. If each employee's period of service and unpaid amounts are organized in advance, claims for substitute payments and the filing of claims after the application move faster, and conflict during the winding-up process is reduced.

If the company's assets are scattered through seizures while the decision is put off, the share that goes to employees shrinks too. If you are thinking of your employees, there are cases where you should actually consider bringing forward the timing of the wind-up.
